description: Eight polygon sequencers on a shared circle: a pointer steps around by a fixed angle and each polygon fires when the pointer passes one of its corners

params.text: Runs its polygon; while it is off that polygon fires nothing and is not drawn
Sets how many corners its polygon has, 1 to 32, spread evenly around the circle
Turns the whole polygon around the circle, 0 to 359 degrees
Adds to the angle between neighbouring corners of its polygon, 0 to 359 degrees, which opens the shape out into a star or a spiral
Sends the pointer back to zero degrees
Sets how far the pointer turns on each clock, 0 to 90 degrees
Fires a polygon only when the pointer lands exactly on one of its corners, rather than whenever it passes one

inputs.text: Runs its polygon above 0V and stops it below, overriding the On button
Sets the corner count of its polygon, 3.2 corners per volt, and overrides the VT knob while patched
Sets the rotation of its polygon, 36 degrees per volt, and overrides the Rot knob while patched
Sets the skew of its polygon, 36 degrees per volt, and overrides the Skew knob while patched
A rising edge sends the pointer back to zero degrees and blocks the clock for 1ms
Each rising edge turns the pointer on by the angle set by Degree
Sets the step angle, 9 degrees per volt over 0-10V, and overrides the Degree knob while patched

outputs.text: A 0.1 second trigger each time the pointer passes a corner of its polygon
Passes the clock through while its polygon was hit on this clock
Carries 10V from a hit on its polygon until the next clock
A 0.1 second trigger on the channel of each polygon as the pointer passes one of its corners, with as many channels as the highest numbered polygon switched on
Passes the clock through on the channel of each polygon that was hit on this clock
Carries 10V on the channel of each polygon that was hit, until the next clock

notes: the circle draws every polygon that is switched on in its own colour, with the pointer as a white line
all eight tracks come up switched off, so nothing fires until a track's On button is pressed or its On input is raised
